label: Coinitial descent of moments
definition: Coinitial c holds when for every moment s strictly earlier than c 0 some member c n of the sequence lies strictly earlier than s. With Descent c (c (n + 1) < c n for all n) this says the sequence runs back below every moment of the past of c 0: it does not accumulate at or above any earlier moment. In ordinary language: one station per past day, back through the whole past, as in an integer-time history (c n = t - n). Counterexample: t, t/2, t/4, ... in non-negative rational time is a descent but not coinitial, since it never goes below 0.
note: Analyst order-theoretic definition; attribution deferred. A coinitial descent from t exists only if the past of t has no beginning (GrimReaperPatchwork notBegunOfCoinitial). It is not a metric notion: in the open-below rational interval (0, 1] the descent 1, 1/2, 1/4, ... is coinitial, though the past is metrically finite. A metric restriction (stations needing slots of a minimum length) is MetricGrimReaper.SlotsAtLeast; in linear time every spaced descent is coinitial (coinitialOfSpaced), not conversely.
